content:
Given the information that I am going to share:
 1) the full text of the publication that you have to extract pretrained model mentions from.

Please return a JSON object with a "model_mentions" key containing an array of objects where each object has the following structure:
- `model_name`: The name of the pretrained model/checkpoint. If not found, set it to "n/a".
- `version`: The version/checkpoint tag, if stated. If not found, set it to "n/a".
- `mention_type`: "created" (paper's own new model), "used" (existing pretrained model used as-is), "fine-tuned" (existing pretrained model fine-tuned/adapted on the paper's own data), or "n/a" if unclear.
- `url`: The URL/repository link for this model, if given (any kind -- Hugging Face Hub, TensorFlow Hub, PyTorch Hub, ModelScope, Civitai, a lab homepage, etc., not just Hugging Face). If not found, set it to "n/a".
- `context_from_paper`: The relevant text passage that mentions this model. If not found, set it to "n/a".

Please follow these strict instructions:
- The output must be a valid JSON object with a "model_mentions" key.
- The "model_mentions" value must be an array of objects.
- Each object must contain the keys `model_name`, `version`, `mention_type`, `url`, and `context_from_paper`.
- Each object must represent exactly ONE distinct model mention. If multiple different models are mentioned, create a separate object for each.
- A model mention does NOT need a URL or version to be valid -- most real mentions have neither. Do not skip a model just because it has no link.
- Any other output format will be considered invalid.

Below is the input data that you will use to generate the output:
1) content => {content}.
